--- WORKED 2026-08-04, CARD STAYS OPEN ---
The card said 'REMINDERS_EMAIL_FROM must be listed in boot validation for BOTH apps - verify it, do not assume it'. Verified by walking the path, and the real defect sat next door to the one described.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG: apps/web's only boot assertion was in app/api/inngest/route.ts, which is loaded for Inngest-driven work. Staff invites are not Inngest-driven - lib/admin/staff.ts -> lib/invites/email.ts -> sendEmail in lib/reminders/clients.ts - a chain that never touches that route. So arming INVITES_LIVE_SEND with REMINDERS_EMAIL_FROM or RESEND_API_KEY absent booted clean, providerConfigured() returned false, and every invite silently degraded to the temporary-password hand-off: no email, no error, no boot signal. The owner would have seen invites 'working' while nothing was ever sent. Exactly the fails-at-the-user-not-at-boot class #763 removed from the reminder path, surviving on the invite path because the sweep followed the reminder path only - which is what this card exists to record.

VERIFIED AND CORRECTLY LEFT ALONE: apps/api asserts on REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND alone, and that is right rather than an omission. apps/api has no invite path at all ('the only body this app can send is patient activation'), so INVITES_LIVE_SEND would be meaningless there. Adding it would have looked like symmetry and meant nothing. The card's 'BOTH apps' framing is therefore superseded: the gap was two send paths inside ONE app, not two apps.

STILL OPEN, and why this card is not shipped: the DoR's 'every var' is the whole portal surface and only the notification path has now been walked twice. Fallback 6 (activation.ts:117) still closes with W13-03's ruling on sendPatientActivation, which is blocked behind LOOP 1.

evidence.ref: #777 MERGED 2026-08-04T15:25:07Z, branch board/LE-darkmode-ink-token, squashed to 0158af7 on origin/main. docs/board/board.css only. Both defects closed and MEASURED, not eyeballed: white ink on the seven dark-mode accent fills scored 2.08:1 to 2.88:1, every one failing WCAG AA 4.5:1; the --on-accent token scores 6.58:1 to 9.13:1 on the same seven. Light mode is byte-identical (the token resolves to #ffffff). color-scheme is now restated in both [data-theme] blocks, so UA surfaces (scrollbars, native selects, date pickers) follow the viewer's toggle instead of the OS. Verified against the RENDERED output, since render-board.mjs inlines the CSS: 0 hardcoded #fff, 0 leftover #170a12, 4 --on-accent declarations, 4 --stakeholder declarations, 7 consumption sites, 2 color-scheme restatements.

cards.notes:
Found during the board-parity work and DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED there, because both defects are visible changes to the platform board's dark mode and fixing them inside a byte-parity ticket would make the diff unreviewable: a reviewer could no longer tell an intended generalisation from an unrelated colour edit. Two defects. (1) `color-scheme: light dark` is declared only on `:root` (board.css:22) and never restated per [data-theme], so scrollbars, native select popups and date pickers follow the OS rather than the viewer's toggle. (2) Hard-coded #fff on light dark-mode fills, seven sites: board.css:216 .btn.primary (on dark --brand #45b9a7), board.css:287 .pips button.pass (for system-dark viewers who never touched the toggle - the #170a12 patch at board.css:286 is scoped to :root[data-theme="dark"] only), and the five .segrow.status button[aria-pressed="true"] fills at board.css:461-465 (shipped, blocked, in_flight, halted, todo). The fix is one theme-driven ink token used in all seven places, the same job --brand-ink already does for brand-tinted surfaces. Also worth folding in while there: two person-coupled sites that survived the parity work untouched because the additive-only rule forbade editing an existing declaration - board.css:323 colours the rodica_batch lane RAIL with var(--rodica), so on this board the STAKEHOLDER FEEDBACK lane wears a person's colour for a person who is not on it, and board.css:395 colours the `stakeholder` gate badge the same way, which five cards on this board carry. Neither is wrong-looking today; both are a token whose name has outlived its meaning.

--- CLOSED 2026-08-04 (#777) ---
The card's line citations for the two person-coupled sites were WRONG and were re-derived rather than transcribed: board.css:323 and :395 as written, 325 and 399 in fact. The seven #fff citations were correct.

Both were fixed with ONE token each rather than seven patches. --on-accent is deliberately not --ink: --ink is text on paper, --on-accent is text on a filled accent, and the two move in OPPOSITE directions between themes, which is why a single literal could never be right in both. --stakeholder carries the identical value to --rodica in both themes, so the role/person split is a rename by indirection with zero visual change; --rodica stays for the two sites that really do mean the person.

The deleted :root[data-theme="dark"] .pips button.pass patch was itself the shape of the bug: it fixed the gate pip only for viewers who had touched the toggle and left every system-dark viewer on 2.41:1.

ONE FINDING DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: light-mode --todo (#a86f10) with white ink is 4.25:1 and already failed 4.5:1 before this PR. Fixing it means changing a light-mode palette VALUE, which is a visible redesign rather than a tokenisation - and silently altering the light palette inside a dark-mode ticket is the same mistake this card was created to avoid. Flagged, not folded in.

cards.title: Shard the Playwright e2e gate across three runners, required check name held stable

evidence.ref: #774 MERGED 2026-08-04 (5fc88a2). MEASURED, not estimated, on run 30942125889 - the first run where all three shards completed on one commit with the isolation defect fixed: shard 1 6m43s, shard 2 6m58s, shard 3 7m10s, aggregate gate 3s. Wall clock ~7m13s, and the number to quote is the SLOWEST shard, never the average. Against the same day's unsharded runs on real code changes (12m30s, 13m00s, 13m22s, 13m57s, 14m08s) that is roughly a 45% cut. The split is now even - 27s between fastest and slowest - where before the fix it ran 6m27s to 13m22s because shard 3 was spending 6.3 minutes on doomed retries, which is exactly why no figure was quoted earlier. Required check name held: 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB)' reported and passed as the aggregate, and branch protection needed NO change - the hard constraint on the whole design.

cards.notes:
Not a Wave 13 loop. Infrastructure that pays back across every PR of the wave, dispatched by the owner before LOOP 1.

THE CONSTRAINT: branch protection pins three contexts by exact string, and a check context IS a job name. Sharding the existing job in place would have renamed its checks to 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB) (1)' and friends; the required context would never report again and every PR would hang forever on a check that no longer exists. So the work moved to a job named 'E2E shard' and a new aggregate job inherits the exact old name, runs no tests, and fails unless all three shards succeeded. NO REPOSITORY SETTINGS CHANGE IS NEEDED - which was the stated fallback condition.

Workflow file and matrix only: zero test-file edits, zero playwright.config.ts edits, retries untouched (no --retries flag on pull_request, so the config's CI ? 2 : 0 still governs).

VERIFIED FROM SOURCE, NOT ASSUMED: setup runs in every shard. Pinned Playwright 1.60.0, runner/index.js:2443-2465 - the shard filter iterates rootSuite.suites, which holds top-level projects only, and dependency projects are prepended afterwards from the UNFILTERED suite. That is also why the invocation now passes --project=chromium alone: naming setup explicitly promotes it to top-level and puts its tests INTO the shard filter, the one arrangement where a shard could receive no setup tests.

THE RED PATH IS PROVEN, and not by a contrived test. A deliberate forced-failure run was planned; it turned out to be unnecessary because attempt 1 produced the exact scenario that needed proving: shard 3 genuinely failed while shards 1 and 2 passed, and the required check 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB)' went RED in 4 seconds. That is the partial-failure case - one leg red, two green - which is the one that matters and the one a designed-to-work argument could not have settled. `if: always()` plus a strict 'success' comparison behaved exactly as intended. Skipped is deliberately NOT accepted as success; this repo has already been bitten by a green that was really a skip.



--- CORRECTION AND DIAGNOSIS, 2026-08-04. THE EARLIER CHECKPOINT WAS WRONG. ---
Board checkpoint 01 (#776, merged) recorded that the cross-file-dependency hypothesis was CHECKED AND REFUTED. That was WRONG, and it was wrong because the check was too narrow: it asked who else REFERENCES the fixture constant AI_REVIEW_DRAFT, when the question that mattered was who else MUTATES the shared review queue. Correcting it here rather than leaving a merged board claim standing.

THE REAL CAUSE, proven rather than hypothesised. e2e/clinical.spec.ts:169-188 HARD-DELETES AI_DELETE_DRAFT, which fixtures.ts defines as a SECOND draft belonging to the SAME patient, Joao Pereira. e2e/revisao-consulta.spec.ts:36-39 finds its queue row by getByRole("row").filter({hasText: patientName}).first().
Unsharded, clinical.spec.ts runs BEFORE revisao-consulta.spec.ts (file order, c before r), so by the time revisao-consulta reads the queue there is exactly ONE Joao Pereira row and .first() is unambiguous.
Sharded, the local listing puts clinical.spec.ts in SHARD 1 and revisao-consulta.spec.ts in SHARD 3. AI_DELETE_DRAFT is therefore never deleted in shard 3, two Joao Pereira rows sit in the queue, and .first() selects the wrong one - whose Assumir never becomes clickable. Hence a 120s locator.click timeout, three times, 6.3 of the 10.4 minutes, which is also why shard 3 was the long pole.

THIS IS A LATENT TEST-ISOLATION DEFECT THAT SHARDING EXPOSED, NOT ONE IT CREATED. revisao-consulta.spec.ts has always depended on another spec file having run first. Any change to file order would trigger it.

PARKED per the owner ceiling of one working session. The enabling fix is one line in a TEST file - scope the row by data-record-id, exactly as clinical.spec.ts:173 already does, instead of hasText + .first() - and this PR was dispatched with zero test-file edits, so it does not belong here.

UNBLOCK CONDITION, exact: authorise the one-line test-isolation fix to e2e/revisao-consulta.spec.ts as its own PR. Once that is on main, #774 needs no change of its own - re-run its checks and all three shards should go green.
RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: authorise it. The defect is real independently of sharding and the fix makes the test say what it means.

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN AND SURVIVES THE PARK: the required-check name held stable (three new E2E shard (N) contexts appeared, Playwright E2E (seeded DB) kept reporting, branch protection untouched); setup ran in all three shards; and the RED PATH works - one red shard against two green produced a RED required check in 4 seconds.
WHAT IS NOT YET PROVEN: the wall-clock win. Shards 1 and 2 came in at 7m27s and 6m27s against the 13m21s baseline, but shard 3 spent 6.3 minutes on three doomed retries, so no honest speed figure exists until the test is fixed. The number to quote is the SLOWEST shard, never the average.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-04, and the park was the right call ---
Parking it rather than merging on a red run is what produced the correct diagnosis. Merging it green-by-retry would have shipped the shard split on top of a live test-isolation defect and left the next person to find it.

The red path was proven twice over: once by accident on attempt 1 (one red shard against two green produced a RED required check in 4 seconds), and the planned deliberate forced-failure run was never needed.

cards.title: Address the review-queue row by record id, not by patient name

evidence.ref: #785 MERGED 2026-08-04 (0b32eed). Owner-authorised. revisao-consulta.spec.ts now passes in 8.3s with no retry, where in shard 3 it was timing out at 120s three times over. Two files: the spec's locator, plus data-record-id on the review queue's desktop <tr> and mobile <li>.

cards.notes:
A LATENT DEFECT SHARDING EXPOSED, NOT ONE IT CREATED. fixtures.ts seeds TWO drafts for the same patient (AI_REVIEW_DRAFT and AI_DELETE_DRAFT, both Joao Pereira). revisao-consulta.spec.ts found its row by patient NAME and took .first(), which was only ever correct because clinical.spec.ts runs earlier in file order (c before r) and hard-deletes the second one at clinical.spec.ts:169-188. So the spec silently depended on ANOTHER SPEC FILE having run. Renaming a spec, or adding one that sorts between them, would have broken it with no sharding involved.

WIDER THAN A TEST EDIT, and flagged as such at the time: the queue row carried only a React `key`, which never reaches the DOM, so there was nothing addressable. data-record-id was added to the markup, mirroring the attribute the patient Registos tab already uses - which is how clinical.spec.ts:173 targets that very record. Inert: no behaviour, no styling, no data beyond an id already in that row's own links.

SELF-INFLICTED REGRESSION IN BETWEEN, recorded because the lesson is the useful part: putting the attribute on BOTH layouts and then writing an unqualified [data-record-id=...] locator matched two elements - the queue renders desktop table AND mobile list into the DOM at all times, hidden by CSS - and Playwright strict mode refused it. The hook was right; the selector was ambiguous. Qualifying it to tr[...] fixed it. It shipped because an e2e locator change was made without running e2e, the same shape of miss as running a filtered test suite instead of the root gates.
